title: Does Buena Vista Social Club live up to the buzz?  Let’s talk about i...
transcript: Off Broadway's hottest ticket is Buena Vista Social Club, and I finally saw it. So let's talk about it. So I didn't really know what to expect with this one. I had heard a lot of really great things, but I also was not familiar with the Buena Vista Social Club, the band that this show is based on. Because if you don't know, the point of us to Social Club is a real life band, and this is basically a bio jukebox musical of their music and story. And while I did really enjoy this one, I have to say, as far as bio jukebox musicals go, I didn't necessarily feel like this one brought much new to the table. It does do a couple of interesting things. So, for example, the main timeline of the show is in 1996, when the band is being formed, but it also flashes back to and interweaves. These same characters lives in 1956, 40 years earlier, played by a different set of actors. And I have to shout out director Sahima Ali here, because when you're dealing with two different characters, I find it can often get really confusing for the audience to follow along. But personally, I was never confused as to which timeline we were in or which actors were playing which versions of which character. The one area where the show really does innovate is in its musical style. It is all Cuban music, which is a genre of Music we really don't hear much in American theater. And I have to say, all of the performers and musicians in the show are so talented. The musical numbers are high energy, and for me, they are definitely the highlight of the show. There were a lot of points in the show that had the same energy as you would have if you were actually, like, watching a concert. And I mean that in the best way possible. I do wanna note that all of the songs are performed entirely in Spanish. So if that is something that bothers you, the show probably won't be for you. But it absolutely did not bother me. And even though I didn't understand what they were saying, I always understood the emotion of the scene that they were trying to convey. And obviously a lot of that credit goes to, again, the performers, the director and also book writer Marco Ramirez. The only other qualm I really had with the show is that I definitely think it helps if you are familiar with Cuban history. Well, I was never completely lost as to what was going on. There were definitely moments in the show where I felt like I wasn't understanding the full gravity of the situation. Because I wasn't familiar with the political climate at the time. But honestly, even knowing nothing about Cuban history, knowing nothing about Buena Vista Social Club, and not really knowing much about this musical style, I Still really, really enjoyed the show. Overall, I'm going to give it a four out of five stars. It is just such a fun show. I had a great night out at the theater, and I love that it explores a new genre of music that I personally have never heard on a New York stage before.
